atoms.sound: Rocco and Cammy are eating lunch together. See what happens when they talk about what food they brought to eat.

feedback.end: That’s right, Rocco is feeling disgust. He thinks eating flies is yucky.

atoms.text:
Disgust is a feeling everyone has. You can feel disgust because of something you see, touch, smell, taste or hear.

Sometimes, disgust is important for our safety. Feeling disgust when smelling rotten food, for example, can protect us from getting sick because we won’t eat the mouldy food!

instruction.text: Find different parts of Rocco to see how he and others can experience disgust.

feedback.end: Many people show disgust with their hands and even their whole body. The hands fold into the body and the fingers clench – almost as if they are protecting themselves from the thing that disgusts them.

Some people squish their eyes together, and their cheeks pull up, making their face look a little squashed. Eyebrows can also show a lot of disgust. One can go up, the other down, or they both furrow in the middle of your face.
An upset tummy is also a common feeling when someone experiences disgust. If you see something that disgusts you, you might not want to eat for a while.
Disgust is also something you show with your mouth. Some people squeeze their lips together, others stick out their tongue.

atoms.text:
Every single person has experienced disgust at some point in their life. It’s one of our most basic instincts, but what causes someone to feel disgust is unique. What makes you feel this way?

This boy, for example, doesn’t like picking up Frodo’s poo when they go on walks together!

atoms.a: Choose the child who is feeling disgust.
